title: Fair play and substantial justice
summary: The fairness inquiry evaluates whether exercising jurisdiction is reasonable in light of the burdens and interests identified in the personal-jurisdiction cases. It operates within the governing jurisdictional framework.
notes: Convenience or a sympathetic plaintiff cannot alone replace the required jurisdictional connection. Asahi also illustrates that substantial burdens can defeat jurisdiction even where contacts are assumed or disputed.

sections.Meaning: The fairness inquiry evaluates whether exercising jurisdiction is reasonable in light of the burdens and interests identified in the personal-jurisdiction cases. It operates within the governing jurisdictional framework.
sections.How to work through the question: Consider the defendant’s burden, the forum’s interest, the plaintiff’s interest in effective relief, efficient resolution, and the relevant shared policy interests. In international cases, consider the distinct burdens and interests discussed in Asahi. Explain the concrete facts supporting each consideration.
